title: SREV-007 service start broker policy posture

scm_access_shape.description: OpenSCManager requires SC_MANAGER_CONNECT against SCM security descriptor; OpenServiceW checks the service object security descriptor against caller token; StartServiceW requires SERVICE_START on the handle

impersonation_topology.description: ServiceServer::Handler calls PipeServer::ImpersonateCaller before dispatching MSGID_SERVICE_START so OpenSCManager/OpenService/StartService run under the impersonated client token

open_policy_question.description: The current policy is SCM DACL delegation while impersonating the caller; a stricter Sandboxie policy must name a new owner such as admin-only, explicit allowlist, or configurable sandbox rule

decision_boundary.description: A blind IsAdmin or elevation-style gate would be stricter than Windows service DACL semantics and could break legitimate non-admin service-start flows

owner_invariant.description: SREV-006B service-name gate already prevents malformed names reaching SCM; SREV-007 documents the current SCM DACL delegation contract and rejects silent admin-only replacement

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime smoke must prove sandboxed non-admin caller without SERVICE_START on the target service receives ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED and identify any supported non-admin service-start flow relying on deliberate DACL grants

contracts: OpenSCManager requires SC_MANAGER_CONNECT against the SCM security descriptor
OpenServiceW grants service object access based on the service security descriptor
StartServiceW requires SERVICE_START on the service handle and fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED otherwise
Sandboxie StartHandler runs under impersonated caller token via PipeServer::ImpersonateCaller
StartHandler documents SCM DACL delegation as the current authorization owner under caller impersonation
No code change replaces SCM DACL semantics with admin-only or elevation-style checks without compatibility evidence
If Sandboxie chooses a stricter policy, the patch must name the new owner: admin-only, explicit StartService allowlist, or configurable rule
